classes.label: Disjointness violation
classes.description: An entity is asserted to belong to two or more classes that are declared disjoint.

classes.label: Functional property conflict
classes.description: A functional property is assigned two or more values that are explicitly distinct.

classes.label: Domain or range violation
classes.description: A relation is used with a subject or object that falls outside its intended domain or range.

classes.label: Cardinality violation
classes.description: A graph violates an explicit cardinality constraint or omits a required property.

classes.label: Temporal impossibility
classes.description: A graph violates a constraint on temporal order.

classes.label: Grounding error
classes.description: A triple is not supported by the source sentence.

notes: Under OWL, a functional property conflict is inconsistent only when the values are asserted to be distinct or are distinct literals.
A missing value for a minimum cardinality constraint is not an OWL inconsistency, because OWL adopts open world assumption.
Revisions after the pilot annotation will be recorded as a new version.
